source_english.description: Bicycle Crunch curls the ribs toward the pelvis from a supine bent-knee position.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Brace and curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
Pause without pulling the neck.
Lower the torso slowly to the support.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable curl range and reduce the decline or load before the neck or back loses control.

selected_scene.pose: Supine on mat, pelvis supported, shoulders curled and torso rotated toward LEFT knee. Both hips and knees remain bent around 90 degrees, shins in tabletop; RIGHT nonworking leg stays bent.

source_english.description: A weighted push-up adds external load across the upper back while the body lowers and presses as one rigid plank.
instructions: Place the weight securely across the upper back and start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Brace the core and lower the chest by bending the elbows while keeping the body straight.
Pause just above the floor, then press through the palms to return to the plank.
End the set before the load shifts or the hips sag.
source_english.safety_note: Use a spotter or secure loading method for the weight and stop if it shifts.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.

source_english.description: Hold the anchored bar at one shoulder and press it diagonally forward before lowering and changing arms.
instructions: Stand beside the anchored end of a barbell and hold its sleeve at one shoulder with one hand.
Use a split stance and keep the free hand on the hip.
Press the bar diagonally forward until the working elbow is straight.
Lower the sleeve to the shoulder, then change arms.

Stop short of a forced lockout.

attempt_history.name: Nordic Hamstrings Curls

source_english.description: Nordic hamstring curls lower the body forward from tall kneeling while the ankles stay anchored and the hamstrings resist the descent.
instructions: Kneel tall with the ankles secured and the hips extended.
Brace the abdomen and keep the body in a straight line from knees to head.
Lean forward slowly by resisting with the hamstrings.
Catch yourself with the hands near the floor, then use assistance to return upright.
form_cues: Use the hands only as needed.
common_mistakes: Trying to force a full range without control.
source_english.safety_note: Anchor the ankles securely and use a range you can stop safely with the hands.

source_english.description: Nordic hamstring curls lower the body forward from tall kneeling while the ankles stay anchored and the hamstrings resist the descent.
instructions: Kneel tall with the ankles secured and the hips extended.
Brace the abdomen and keep the body in a straight line from knees to head.
Lean forward slowly by resisting with the hamstrings.
Catch yourself with the hands near the floor, then use assistance to return upright.
form_cues: Use the hands only as needed.
common_mistakes: Trying to force a full range without control.
source_english.safety_note: Anchor the ankles securely and use a range you can stop safely with the hands.

source_english.description: Pull from a hang and transition the torso over the bar before pressing to support.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chest is above the bar and your arms are fully flexed.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kip controlled as the chest rises over the bar before the press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Pull from a hang and transition the torso over the bar before pressing to support.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chest is above the bar and your arms are fully flexed.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kip controlled as the chest rises over the bar before the press.

instructions: Set the machine so the hips are supported and the feet or legs are secured.

source_english.description: The Butterfly (Pec Deck) opens and closes the arms around the chest with a soft elbow bend rather than turning the motion into a press.
instructions: Set up on the machine with a soft bend in the elbows and the chest supported as required.
Open the arms only as far as the shoulders remain comfortable.
Bring the hands together by squeezing the chest without changing the elbow angle.
Return slowly to the starting position.
form_cues: Move through the chest, not the wrists.
common_mistakes: Turning the movement into a press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and stop before the shoulder reaches an uncomfortable stretch.

selected_scene.grip: Hands relaxed alongside prescribed forearm contacts; elbow/forearm pads carry load, no invented cable handle.

source_english.description: The Calf Extension (Machine) lowers and raises the heels through a deliberate calf stretch and contraction while the feet stay aligned.
instructions: Set up on the machine with the balls of the feet supported and the legs aligned.
Lower the heels slowly to feel a calf stretch.
Press through the big-toe side of the foot to rise as high as controlled.
Pause at the top, then repeat.
common_mistakes: Using the knees to create the motion.
source_english.safety_note: Avoid bouncing at the bottom, especially when the calf or Achilles is stiff.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Adjust the seat of the leverage machine so that your shoulders are aligned with the lever pad.
Place your toes on the lever pad, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or side supports for stability.
Push the lever pad down by extending your ankles, contracting your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position by allowing your heels to rise back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: The Chest Fly (Machine) opens and closes the arms around the chest with a soft elbow bend rather than turning the motion into a press.
instructions: Set up on the machine with a soft bend in the elbows and the chest supported as required.
Open the arms only as far as the shoulders remain comfortable.
Bring the hands together by squeezing the chest without changing the elbow angle.
Return slowly to the starting position.

source_english.description: Crunch (Machine) curls the ribs toward the pelvis from a seated machine position.
instructions: Sit against the machine pad with feet secured and hands on the handles.
Brace the abdomen and curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
Pause without pulling the neck.
Return the pad or torso slowly to upright.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable curl range and reduce the decline or load before the neck or back loses control.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Sit on the leverage machine with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles or place your hands on the side pads for support.
Engage your abs and slowly lean back, allowing the pad to move with you.
Once your upper body is at a 45-degree angle, contract your abs and crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Crunch (Machine) curls the ribs toward the pelvis from a seated machine position.
instructions: Sit against the machine pad with feet secured and hands on the handles.
Brace the abdomen and curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
Pause without pulling the neck.
Return the pad or torso slowly to upright.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable curl range and reduce the decline or load before the neck or back loses control.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Sit on the leverage machine with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles or place your hands on the side pads for support.
Engage your abs and slowly lean back, allowing the pad to move with you.
Once your upper body is at a 45-degree angle, contract your abs and crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Glute Ham Raise lowers the straight body from a secured support and curls it back using the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Secure the ankles and position the hips on the glute-ham support.
Brace the trunk and lower the torso in a straight line.
Curl the body back up by squeezing the hamstrings and glutes.
Return without hyperextending the lower back.
source_english.safety_note: Use assistance or a shortened eccentric until the hips stay extended.

selected_scene.pose: Body straight knees-to-head with hips extended, knees supported on GHR pad and feet/ankles secured; torso lowered toward horizontal without hip hinge.
selected_scene.grip: Arms crossed over chest, a published explicit option.

selected_scene.movement_trajectory: Lower straight body forward about supported knees, then flex knees to curl body back up; hips stay extended.
selected_scene.camera: Full-body front-side three-quarter view exposing every prescribed contact, grip and support. Entire person and all equipment visible within square; no crop, text, arrows or second phase.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Adjust the glute-ham raise machine to fit your body.
Position yourself face down on the machine with your ankles secured.
Place your hands on your chest or cross them over your chest.
Engage your hamstrings and glutes to lift your upper body up towards the ceiling.
Continue lifting until your body is in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Hack Squat (Machine) bends the hips and knees through a sled-supported squat path before returning to standing.
instructions: Stand with the sled machine and feet about shoulder-width apart.
Bend the hips and knees to the controlled depth while keeping both feet planted.

instructions: Set up the machine so the working leg can move away from the midline without rotating the pelvis.

Pause briefly at the end without leaning away.
Return slowly and complete the planned repetitions on each side.

source_english.description: Pull Up (Assisted) pulls from a controlled hang until the chin reaches or clears the bar, then lowers under control.

source_english.description: Face down on the machine, lift the legs by extending the hips and lower them under control.
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to fit your body and secure your feet in the foot pads.
Lie face down on the machine with your upper body hanging off the edge and your hips resting on the pad.
Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the abdomen on the pad while the legs extend behind the hips.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Sit at the calf machine with the forefeet on the platform and raise both heels before lowering them below the start.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are slightly bent and your feet are flat on the footplate.
Place your toes on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the seat for stability.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.

source_english.description: Sit at the calf machine with the forefeet on the platform and raise both heels before lowering them below the start.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are slightly bent and your feet are flat on the footplate.
Place your toes on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the seat for stability.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ankle over the second toe.
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.
source_english.safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.

source_english.description: Sit against the leg-curl back pad and draw both lower legs toward the hamstrings under the ankle lever before lowering them.

Place your lower legs under the padded lever, just above your ankles.

Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings.

source_english.description: Reverse Curl (Cable) curls the palms-down weight toward the shoulders while keeping the upper arms still.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the low cable and stand facing the machine with knees softly bent.
Grip the bar with an overhand reverse-curl grip and keep the elbows beside the ribs.
Curl the bar toward the shoulders without moving the upper arms.
Pause, then lower the bar slowly until the elbows are straight.
form_cues: Use a steady squeeze at the top.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a load that keeps the wrists and elbows aligned without momentum.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: A standing cable glute kickback extends one hip backward against a low cable while the pelvis stays square.
instructions: Attach the ankle cuff to a low pulley and face the machine with one hand on the support.
Brace the trunk and keep the standing leg slightly bent.
Drive the cuffed leg straight backward from the hip without arching the back.
Pause, return the foot slowly, and switch sides.
form_cues: Keep the body aligned for the apparatus.
Move through the hip-extension path smoothly.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Changing the stance during the repetition.
Using momentum instead of the target muscles.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load and range that let you maintain the exercise position throughout.

Place the cable around your ankle and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight throughout the exercise.
Slowly extend your leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat with the other leg.

source_english.description: A standing cable glute kickback extends one hip backward against a low cable while the pelvis stays square.
instructions: Attach the ankle cuff to a low pulley and face the machine with one hand on the support.
Brace the trunk and keep the standing leg slightly bent.
Drive the cuffed leg straight backward from the hip without arching the back.
Pause, return the foot slowly, and switch sides.
form_cues: Keep the body aligned for the apparatus.
Move through the hip-extension path smoothly.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Changing the stance during the repetition.
Using momentum instead of the target muscles.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load and range that let you maintain the exercise position throughout.

source_english.description: Cable Twist (Down to up) rotates a standing trunk from one outside hip to the opposite shoulder against a cable.
instructions: Set the cable at low height and stand sideways with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handle with both hands beside the outside hip and brace the abdomen.
Rotate the ribs upward to the opposite shoulder while the feet stay planted.
Return along the same diagonal, then turn around for the other side.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and keep the cable's diagonal path clear of the body.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

source_english.description: Hip Abduction (Cable) moves one leg away from the body's midline against cable while the pelvis stays level.
instructions: Set up the cable attachment so the working leg can move away from the midline without rotating the pelvis.
Brace the trunk and move the leg outward through a controlled range.
Pause briefly at the end without leaning away.
Return slowly and complete the planned repetitions on each side.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop before the hip pinches or the pelvis tilts.

source_english.description: Stand beside the low pulley and raise one arm outward to shoulder height before lowering and switching sides.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with one hand, palm facing down, and stand far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.
Keep your arm straight and slowly raise it out to the side until it is parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

source_english.description: Stand beside the low pulley and raise one arm outward to shoulder height before lowering and switching sides.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with one hand, palm facing down, and stand far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.
Keep your arm straight and slowly raise it out to the side until it is parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Stand at the high pulley and press one handle down beside the ribs by extending the elbow, then switch arms.
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment at chest height.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cable.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Start with your arm fully extended and perpendicular to the floor.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and push the bar down until your arm is fully extended.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

source_english.description: Decline Bench Press (Machine) is a supported chest press using the barbell.
instructions: Lie on a declined bench with feet secured. Grip the barbell and hold it over the chest.
Lower the resistance toward the chest with elbows controlled.
Pause without bouncing or losing shoulder position.
Press back to straight arms, then rerack or set the weights down safely.
source_english.safety_note: Use a spotter or safeties for the loaded press and stop before shoulder control is lost.

source_english.description: Decline Bench Press (Machine) is a supported chest press using the barbell.
instructions: Lie on a declined bench with feet secured. Grip the barbell and hold it over the chest.
Lower the resistance toward the chest with elbows controlled.
Pause without bouncing or losing shoulder position.
Press back to straight arms, then rerack or set the weights down safely.
source_english.safety_note: Use a spotter or safeties for the loaded press and stop before shoulder control is lost.

source_english.description: The Chest Dip (Assisted) lowers the body by bending the elbows between parallel supports, then presses back up while the shoulders remain controlled.
instructions: Mount the parallel handles with arms straight and the torso slightly inclined.
Bend the elbows to lower until the upper arms approach parallel with the floor.
Pause before the shoulders lose control.
Press through the handles to straighten the elbows and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use the assistance platform or a lighter load if the full dip depth cannot stay controlled.

source_english.description: The Chest Dip (Assisted) lowers the body by bending the elbows between parallel supports, then presses back up while the shoulders remain controlled.
instructions: Mount the parallel handles with arms straight and the torso slightly inclined.
Bend the elbows to lower until the upper arms approach parallel with the floor.
Pause before the shoulders lose control.
Press through the handles to straighten the elbows and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use the assistance platform or a lighter load if the full dip depth cannot stay controlled.

source_english.description: A ski erg uses a standing hinge and a simultaneous downward pull on the handles to drive the flywheel.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with feet hip-width apart and grasp one handle in each hand.
Reach the arms overhead while keeping the spine long and knees softly bent.
Hinge at the hips and pull both handles down toward the thighs in a strong, smooth stroke.
Allow the arms to rise under control as the hips return to the starting hinge.
form_cues: Finish the pull at the thighs.
Use the hips and lats together.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the handles clear of your body and use a resistance that allows a smooth return.

selected_scene.single_phase: End of the simultaneous double-pole drive, before controlled recovery
selected_scene.pose: Stand facing a vertical SkiErg, feet hip-width apart on the stable floor stand. Hips move back into a controlled hinge, knees softly bent, torso inclined forward, spine long. Arms finish alongside hips with small remaining elbow bend; hands near the thighs. No seated rower or deep squat.
selected_scene.grip: One ski handle firmly held in each hand; neutral wrists, thumbs toward the thighs at the finish. Both hands drive together, no alternating classic-ski variant.
selected_scene.supports_and_equipment: Both bare feet remain planted on the published floor-stand base, no seat, no knee pad or foot straps. Standard compatible unbranded SkiErg frame with paired overhead drive-cord exits, one taut continuous synthetic cord to each handle and an intact flywheel housing; no extra ankle cuffs or bar attachment.
selected_scene.movement_trajectory: Simultaneously pull both handles downward toward the thighs by coordinated hip hinge and arm drive. Hinge precedes knee bend; avoid deep squat, arm-only pull, locked elbows or snapping recovery. Return upright and raise handles smoothly for the next stroke; render only the single finish phase.
selected_scene.camera: Full-body front-side three-quarter view exposing every prescribed contact, grip and support. Entire person and all equipment visible within square; no crop, text, arrows or second phase.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Adjust the seat height and footrests to a comfortable position.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Sit up straight with your feet flat on the footrests.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your triceps and push the handles down towards your thighs.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: A ski erg uses a standing hinge and a simultaneous downward pull on the handles to drive the flywheel.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with feet hip-width apart and grasp one handle in each hand.
Reach the arms overhead while keeping the spine long and knees softly bent.
Hinge at the hips and pull both handles down toward the thighs in a strong, smooth stroke.
Allow the arms to rise under control as the hips return to the starting hinge.
form_cues: Finish the pull at the thighs.
Use the hips and lats together.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the handles clear of your body and use a resistance that allows a smooth return.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
